**Visual analysis:**

- **Affected part**: Stem — longitudinal cross-section
- **Key features**:
  - Dark brown to black streaking running through the internal vascular/xylem tissue
  - Outer green cortex is intact and healthy-looking
  - Discoloration is confined to the vascular bundles and pith, running lengthwise
  - No soft rot, no external lesions, no fungal growth visible

**Reasoning through classes:**

The defining feature here is **internal vascular discoloration** (dark brown/black streaking in xylem tissue) visible only when the stem is cut longitudinally. The outer cortex remains green.

- **Verticillium Wilt**: Classic diagnostic sign is exactly this — dark brown discoloration of xylem/vascular tissue in a longitudinal stem cut, while outer tissue stays intact. High match.
- **Bacterial Wilt / Southern Bacterial Wilt**: Would show milky bacterial ooze when cut, not dry dark streaking.
- **Bacterial Canker and Wilt of Tomato**: Can cause internal browning but usually accompanied by external cankers/streaks.
- **Southern Blight, Sclerotinia**: Affect the outer stem (cortex collapse, white mycelium, sclerotia) — not matching.

The dry, dark brown-to-black vascular streaking in the internal xylem with intact outer cortex is the textbook hallmark of Verticillium wilt.
